title: Retrieval vs generation
summary: An unsupported answer can fail at different stages requiring different fixes.

sections.label: Diagnosis
rows: Was the needed permitted evidence found?
Does the answer accurately use and support itself with that evidence?
Does the claim answer this question within the required scope and conditions?

sections.label: Research example
sections.text: RAGChecker separates retrieval and generation diagnosis with claim-level evaluation. Use the principle even if you do not adopt that implementation.

sections.label: Acceptance
sections.text: Fix missing evidence or wrong selection before assuming a larger model will resolve every unsupported answer.

sections.label: Gap review: workflow use and checks
items: Recommended use: Locate whether an unsupported result failed at retrieval, selection, generation or applicability.
Record the needed source passage and whether retrieval returned it.
Compare support of the final claim with the selected passage and required scope.
Workflow placement and checks are Atlas recommendations. Existing examples, tenant availability, older product claims and comparative benefits were not revalidated by this mapping review.

catalog.applicability: Use when an answer is unsupported and you need to tell whether the evidence was never found, the wrong passage or version was selected, the generation misused it, or the claim falls outside the required scope, before reaching for a larger model.
catalog.limits: Reading a topic does not configure tools, execute a workflow or establish passing evidence.
